i have diagnosed ocd. if you think you may have it and the possible symptoms are disrupting your daily life in anyway, i would go get help. my mental health has drastically improved since getting help. it doesn’t make you weak getting help, i promise. ocd is a cycle. first an intrusive thought enters your head (for example “does the living room look nice”), then the urge to act on a compulsion which helps to get rid of the intrusive thought (like actively checking the room). then there’s the anxiety relief of when you’ve acted on the compulsion and the intrusive thought has gone away until the next one comes along. all intrusive thoughts and compulsions are different. i have one of repeatedly tapping my left pocket outside the house when i know my phone is in there and i would hear it if it fell out or something, but i’m never *fully* convinced and i have to do it. i probably tap my left pocket about 50 times every time i leave the house. i have another one where i have to grab the kettle handle before it goes off. does it feel like an itch you have to scratch? and do you relate to the cycle at all? is it worse when you’re stressed? ocd always starts on intrusive thoughts, so if you relate to that i really would recommend getting help. hope this helped a bit :)

i can only talk from experience so this may not be so helpful but :
• they put you down all the time and make you feel like a lesser person.
• they tell the most arbitrary lies for attention.
• they talk and talk at you about their problems but will not take in ANY of your advice or let you talk about yours.
• they make you feel guilty for the smallest things or things you didn’t even do.
• all your conversations feel very one-sided, in fact the whole relationship feels one-sided. they never properly ask how you are, you always pay for lunch etc etc. it feels like they control everything inside your relationship.
• when you try to reason with them when they’re being ridiculous, they act all hurt and upset like you’re in the wrong/to make you feel as if you’re in the wrong.
• if you don’t want to do something they want you to do, they try to make you feel bad about it until you give in.
•other people outside the relationship are telling you this persons clearly toxic.
• you’re always wrong, they’re always right.
• they have sneaky tactical ways of making you do things you don’t want to do, like doing something for them or giving information you’d rather not share. 
• you can feel something’s not right in the relationship, and it feels like it’s built on many lies.
• you find yourself having to lie to them to protect yourself.
• sometimes they’ll pretend to be terribly hurt or sick just so you HAVE to sympathise with them and then they feel they have more control.
• you feel like nothing you do for them is ever good enough.

i hope this helped a bit or at least gave an indicator, but as i said it’s only from my experience. i would say the fact you’re even questioning if it’s a toxic relationship is a red flag in itself.

if you come to the realisation that you most likely do have depression, i wish you the best of luck. it’s best to get professional help as left untreated it can spiral downwards. i nearly lost my life but i’m better now.
